name: agent
description: Agent tasks with tools (read, list, write, edit, cmd/PowerShell) in a throwaway folder: fix bugs, implement from a spec, transform data, refactor, use the shell. Graded by checking the folder afterwards. Needs 'run model-written code' (the model runs commands).

tasks.title: Fix an off-by-one bug
tasks.prompt: The tests in test_stats.py fail. Find and fix the bug in stats.py (do not change the tests). Run the tests to confirm they pass.

files.test_stats.py:
from stats import mean, median
assert mean([1, 2, 3]) == 2
assert median([3, 1, 2]) == 2
assert median([4, 1, 3, 2]) == 2.5
print('ok')

check.tests:
import importlib, stats
importlib.reload(stats)
assert stats.median([4,1,3,2]) == 2.5
assert stats.median([10,2,8,4,6,12]) == 7
assert stats.median([5]) == 5
assert stats.mean([2,4]) == 3

tasks.title: Implement from a spec
tasks.prompt: Read SPEC.md and implement the function in roman.py so that it follows the spec exactly.

files.SPEC.md:
# to_roman(n)

Convert an integer 1..3999 to a Roman numeral string (uppercase, subtractive notation: IV, IX, XL, XC, CD, CM).
Raise ValueError for anything outside 1..3999 (including 0 and negative numbers).

check.tests:
import roman
assert roman.to_roman(1994) == 'MCMXCIV'
assert roman.to_roman(3999) == 'MMMCMXCIX'
assert roman.to_roman(4) == 'IV'
assert roman.to_roman(40) == 'XL'
for bad in (0, -5, 4000):
    try:
        roman.to_roman(bad)
        raise AssertionError('no ValueError for %r' % bad)
    except ValueError:
        pass

tasks.prompt: Rename the function get_usr to get_user everywhere in this project (definition and all uses). The program main.py must still print the same output.

files.main.py:
from report import line

print(line(7))
print(get_usr(3)['name'])

tasks.title: Write tests that catch a bug
tasks.prompt: slugify.py contains a function slugify(text). Write test_slugify.py with plain assert statements (no pytest needed) that pass for the current, correct implementation. Good tests should also catch broken versions. Run your test file to confirm it passes.

check.tests:
import shutil, subprocess, sys, os
code = open('test_slugify.py', encoding='utf-8').read()
assert code.count('assert') >= 3, 'needs at least 3 asserts'
def run():
    return subprocess.run([sys.executable, 'test_slugify.py'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10).returncode
shutil.copy('slugify.py', 'slugify.orig')
assert run() == 0, 'tests fail on the correct implementation'
broken = ['import re\ndef slugify(text):\n    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", text.strip()).strip("-")\n',
          'import re\ndef slugify(text):\n    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", text.strip().lower())\n',
          'def slugify(text):\n    return text.strip().lower().replace(" ", "-")\n']
caught = 0
for b in broken:
    open('slugify.py', 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(b)
    if run() != 0: caught += 1
shutil.copy('slugify.orig', 'slugify.py')
assert caught >= 2, 'only %d of 3 broken versions caught' % caught

tasks.title: Fix a crash from its traceback
tasks.prompt: main.py crashes. Run it, read the error, fix the cause in parse.py, and run main.py again until it prints the total.

files.main.py:
from parse import load, total
print(total(load('orders.json')))

check.tests:
import subprocess, sys, json
r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, 'main.py'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
assert r.returncode == 0, r.stderr[-300:]
assert abs(float(r.stdout.strip()) - 26.0) < 1e-9, r.stdout
